text:
maria (infra): Heads-up — Saturday morning euw2 burst caused heavy GPU queueing and near-OOM on several pods. Putting quick timeline + ask here.
ajay (eng): timeline + severity? any errors or just slow tail latency?
maria (infra): peak window 02:08-02:38 UTC. queue depth ~1.2k, tail latency >30s, ~7 pods reported OOM-kill attempts but kube restarted before full OOM. customer-visible 5xx fallbacks for a few endpoints. link to graphs: https://grafana.redwood/euw2/holiday-surge
taku (autoscaler): autoscaler logs show repeated failed scale-ups due to AZ quota limit in eu-west-2: `CreateInstanceQuotaExceeded`. Also saw `scale_cooldown` prevented immediate re-adds.
olivia (sre): KV cache eviction rate jumped at 02:10, which increased token generation time on larger models by ~18%. That amplified load per-request.
maria (infra): suspected root causes: 1) forecast underpredicted promo traffic (~30% higher than plan), 2) AZ quota exhaustion meant we couldn't scale into spare AZs, 3) autoscaler conservatively batched scale decisions (cooldowns + stabilization), 4) routing put a chunk on cheaper, slower model variants.
pete (capacity): impact: emergency spill to on-demand GPUs increased cost (~$12k extra for the 30m window). Operational risk: sustained >95% util reduces headroom for preemption and KV cache stability.
devops-bot: ALERT: node-group euw2-gpu-02 at 95% capacity @ 2026-02-14T02:14:07Z.
jen (support): We saw ~18 customer tickets during the window; most were rate-limit fallbacks. Notified a handful of enterprise customers with transient errors.
carla (product): Which customers were impacted? we need to prioritize outreach.
maria (infra): ETA on a mapping export coming in ~20m. quick fixes we executed: - temporary routing away from slower variants - manual scale-up in unaffected AZs where quotas allowed - increased request timeouts churn limit to avoid client retries.
ajay (eng): logs snippet from pod (02:12):
```
2026-02-14T02:12:08Z WARN token-gen latency ms=4123 kv-eviction=true
2026-02-14T02:12:09Z ERROR allocation failed: insufficient capacity
```
taku (autoscaler): actionable follow-ups I propose: - add burst headroom policy during promotions (+20% reserved) - reduce `scale_down_cooldown` for GPU nodegroups from 300s -> 90s during flash windows - add quota checks in the planner to failover earlier
pete (capacity): also propose AZ-aware buffer: prefer spreading reserved capacity across AZs and pre-warming spot pools in target AZs a day before promos.
olivia (sre): we should add KV cache saturation metric to the incident runbook and alert when eviction rate > X/sec. That would have given earlier signal.
carla (product): For next promo: require capacity bake-in 48h prior and a sync with growth forecasts. Product will share promo list earlier.
jen (support): For comms: suggest templated apology + mitigation + ETA for follow-up. I can draft today.
maria (infra): Open questions: - exact forecast miss vector (model vs. behavioral)? - why routing sent traffic to slower variants instead of throttling? - did autoscaler decisions correlate with AZ quota errors?
ajay (eng): I'll correlate routing decisions with model performance metrics and post a short table.
taku (autoscaler): I'll attach autoscaler timeline + events and add a simulation for cooldown changes.
pete (capacity): I'll request temporary quota increases with cloud and a list of AZs we should pre-warm.
olivia (sre): I'll prototype a KV-eviction alert and add to runbook.
maria (infra): Thanks — let's reconvene tomorrow 10:00 UTC for a retro. Action owners: ajay (routing), taku (autoscaler), pete (capacity), olivia (runbook + alerts), jen (customer comms), carla (promo coordination). :white_check_mark:
ajay (eng): noted. I'll post findings by EOD.
carla (product): I'll start coordinating promo schedule changes.
jen (support): I'll draft comms and share for review.
---
Notes: keep incident thread terse; follow-ups go to smaller threads (capacity ops + autoscaler).
